Car Learning to Act (CARLA)  is another open-source simulator for autonomous driving in urban environments. It can be deployed to train and evaluate the models for self-driving, including perception and control algorithms. CARLA also provides diverse kinds of city layouts and different kinds of vehicles and buildings. The simulator provides different environmental conditions, weather and time, and different sensor suites. According to the setup, the models can be trained and validated within this simulator. Three self-driving approaches are evaluated in CARLA, including generic modular pipeline, end-to-end imitation learning, and end-to-end [...] ### III-B End-to-end Software Systems

Instead of separating the self-driving problem into a few sub-tasks and solving them individually, the end-to-end system integrates all components for a holistic solution. It takes the raw data from sensors as input and uses a single model to process the data and directly output the control commands. As the system is based on a single model, all functions can be trained together. Although the generic modular systems offer good interpretability and maintainability, the overall accuracy is highly dependent on the ability to avoid the errors from each module to propagate through the pipeline . The end-to-end system, however, mitigates this issue by using a single module, reducing the potential for error accumulation. ### Conclusion

The integration of end-to-end continuous integration and delivery pipelines is revolutionizing the development of safety-critical autonomous driving software. By automating and unifying development, testing, compliance, and deployment processes, organizations can deliver safer, more reliable autonomous driving systems at a faster pace.

While challenges remain, adopting best practices and leveraging emerging technologies can mitigate risks and propel autonomous driving innovation to new heights. For developers and stakeholders, embracing sophisticated CI/CD pipelines is not just a technical upgrade but a strategic imperative to build the future of mobility securely and efficiently.

Explore Comprehensive Market Analysis of Autonomous Driving Tool Chain Market [...] ### What is End-to-End CI/CD in Autonomous Driving?

Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery are development practices that emphasize frequent integration of code changes and automated delivery of software updates. An end-to-end CI/CD pipeline for autonomous driving software encompasses all stages from code commit, automated testing, validation, and deployment within a cohesive framework.

This approach enables developers to detect defects early, automate repetitive tasks, and maintain high-quality software at all times. In safety-critical domains like autonomous driving, it is vital to extend these pipelines to incorporate safety analysis, compliance checks, and rigorous testing standards.

### Key Components of an End-to-End CI/CD Pipeline for Autonomous Driving [...] Siddhi Thaware

### Siddhi Thaware

In the rapidly evolving landscape of autonomous driving, software development has taken center stage as a critical enabler of vehicle intelligence and safety. Autonomous driving systems rely heavily on complex software architectures that must not only perform flawlessly but also comply with stringent safety standards. To meet these demands, the integration of end-to-end continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines has become indispensable for developers working on safety-critical autonomous driving software.
